citation: Mah E, Garcia-Campayo V, Liska D (2018). Substitution of Corn Starch with Resistant Starch Type 4 in a Breakfast Bar Decreases Postprandial Glucose and Insulin Responses: A Randomized, Controlled, Crossover Study. Current Developments in Nutrition 2(10):nzy066.
protocol: Two breakfast bars, double-blind crossover: control bar (55 g total carbohydrate, 4 g fibre, 10 g fat, 4 g protein) vs RS4 bar (56 g carbohydrate, 32 g fibre, 10 g fat, 4 g protein). Capillary glucose and venous insulin at -15, -5, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: n=21 healthy adults (11 women), age 34.1 ± 8.6 y, BMI 23.5 ± 2.3 kg/m2 (Table 2, mean ± SD); per-protocol n=20.

reports.where: Table 3: iAUC0-120, Cmax, Tmax per bar
Table 3: iAUC0-120 (µIU/mL × min), Cmax, Tmax per bar

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: corn-starch bar vs RS4 bar at matched total carbohydrate, fat and protein. Second RS4-for-starch swap with a different food and much larger fibre gap than stewart-2017. Watch: Table 3 values are medians with 95% CIs, not means. Only in figures: glucose and insulin time courses.
